headline: Senior-housing strength drives FFO gains, guidance mixed
summary_short: Welltower posted Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS of $0.61 (+35.6% y/y) and normalized FFO per share of $1.60 (+25.0% y/y), with total same-store NOI up 15.5% y/y led by 20.5% growth in Seniors Housing Operating. The board raised the dividend 15% to $0.85.
summary_long: Growth was led by the Seniors Housing Operating (SHO) segment, where same-store NOI rose 20.5% y/y on 330bps of occupancy gains and 5.2% RevPOR growth; total portfolio SSNOI grew 15.5%. Diluted EPS fell sequentially to $0.61 from $1.02 in Q1 because Q1 carried the bulk of H1's $518.9M in real-estate-disposition gains versus $98.5M this quarter (timing, not deterioration). Welltower closed $6.3B of pro rata investments in the quarter ($15.5B YTD/pending) and issued C$1.15B of unsecured notes; net debt to consolidated enterprise value improved to 8.9% from 10.1% y/y. FY2026 guidance: net income per share lowered to $3.11-$3.19 (from $3.24-$3.38); normalized FFO per share raised to $6.36-$6.44 (from $6.21-$6.35). Quarterly dividend raised 15% to $0.85.

drivers.explanation: Company cites Seniors Housing Operating strength (occupancy and RevPOR gains) and accretive capital deployment ($15.5B YTD closed/pending investments) as the primary drivers of the quarter.
SHO portfolio SSNOI grew 20.5% y/y from 330bps of average occupancy growth and 5.2% RevPOR growth, the largest contributor to total 15.5% SSNOI growth.
Diluted EPS fell q/q to $0.61 from $1.02 because Q1 carried most of H1's $518.9M gain on real-estate dispositions, versus only $98.5M recognized in Q2 alone.
Board raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $0.85, citing confidence in the durability of cash flow growth and balance sheet strength.

Company reports leverage steady-to-improving: net debt to consolidated enterprise value fell to 8.9% from 10.1% y/y after sourcing over $4B of capital including equity issuance and disposition proceeds.
